s1.syndrome_frame: A firm mass in the lower outer quadrant of the left breast, fixed to the pectoralis major muscle, with a history of previous breast cancer treatment
salient_findings: 20 mm firm mass fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space on mammography
Lobulated, well-defined mass with heterogeneous internal echoes on ultrasonography
key_facts: 59-year-old woman
Previous breast-conserving surgery with endocrine therapy and radiation to the left breast
Previous carcinoma in the upper inner quadrant of the left breast
Mass is fixed to the pectoralis major muscle
Overlying skin is uninvolved
No palpable axillary lymph nodes
Mammography showed a focal asymmetrical density in the retromammary space
Ultrasonography revealed a lobulated, well-defined mass
Core-needle biopsy suggested atrophic mammary glands
Lesion increased in size on three-month follow-up

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of radiation therapy to the left breast, and the mass is located in the retromammary space, which is a common location for post-radiation sarcomas. The increase in size of the lesion on follow-up also suggests a malignant process.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, primary leiomyosarcoma of the breast is extremely rare, and the patient's history of radiation therapy makes post-radiation sarcoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
rejected.why: This is a type of sarcoma that can occur in the breast, but the patient's history of radiation therapy and the location of the mass make post-radiation sarcoma a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Fibrosarcoma
rejected.why: This is another type of sarcoma that can occur in the breast, but it is less likely given the patient's history and the characteristics of the mass.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: This is a type of breast tumor that can be benign or malignant, but it is less likely given the patient's history of radiation therapy and the location of the mass.
